old: Biotechnology rests on two core techniques. Genetic engineering alters the chemistry of the genetic material. Bioprocess engineering maintains a sterile, contamination-free environment for large-scale culture. Cohen and Boyer made the first recombinant DNA in 1972 by linking an antibiotic resistance gene from a Salmonella typhimurium plasmid into another plasmid. The basic steps are: isolate DNA, cut it with a restriction enzyme, amplify the gene of interest by PCR, ligate it into a vector, transfer it into a host, culture the host and recover the product. Restriction endonucleases recognise palindromic sequences and leave sticky ends that DNA ligase joins. A vector needs three features: an ori, a selectable marker and cloning sites. Recombinants are identified by insertional inactivation, either of an antibiotic resistance gene or of lacZ (blue-white screening). Hosts are made competent with $Ca^{2+}$ and heat shock, or the DNA is delivered by microinjection or a gene gun. The product is then made in bioreactors and purified by downstream processing.

old: Some think Bt toxin is activated by acidic pH or by proteases. The NCERT answer is the alkaline pH of the insect gut, which solubilises the crystals and activates the protoxin.
